description:
Implement worktree-aware storage and claim coordination to enable multiple agents to work on different issues simultaneously on the same machine without conflicts.

## Problem
Current `.jit/` directory is shared, causing file conflicts when multiple agents work in parallel. Need isolated per-worktree state with shared coordination layer.

## Solution Architecture

### Two-Tier Storage Model
- **Per-worktree data plane** (`<worktree>/.jit/`): Issue data, local gates, local events
- **Shared control plane** (`.git/jit/`): Claims registry, locks, heartbeats, control events

### Identity System
- **Agent ID**: Stable identifier (e.g., `agent:copilot-1`)
- **Worktree ID**: Deterministic per-worktree identifier (e.g., `wt:abc123`)
- **Lease ID**: ULID for each claim operation

### Claim/Lease Semantics
- Time-bounded leases with TTL (default 600s)
- Heartbeat mechanism for lease renewal
- Automatic expiration and eviction
- Single-writer policy per issue
- Append-only audit log with derived index

### Read vs Write Operations
- **Leases control writes, not reads**: All issue data remains readable from any worktree regardless of claims
- **Issue creation exempted**: `jit issue create` doesn't require lease (allocates new ULID, no conflict)
- **Query coordination**: `jit query ready` filters claimed issues, other queries aggregate across git + main .jit/

## Implementation Checklist

### Phase 1: Foundation
- [ ] Worktree path detection and resolution
- [ ] Worktree identity assignment and persistence
- [ ] Directory layout migration (`.git/jit/` control plane)
- [ ] Agent identity configuration

### Phase 2: Claim Coordination
- [ ] Claims JSONL append-only log
- [ ] Claims index (derived view with active leases)
- [ ] Atomic claim acquisition with file locking
- [ ] Lease renewal and release operations
- [ ] Automatic expiration and eviction
- [ ] Heartbeat mechanism

### Phase 3: Enforcement
- [ ] Pre-commit hook for structural edit validation
- [ ] Pre-commit hook for global operation gating
- [ ] Branch divergence detection
- [ ] Lease requirement checks

### Phase 4: CLI Surface
- [ ] `jit claim acquire <issue> --ttl <secs>`
- [ ] `jit claim renew <lease-id> --ttl <secs>`
- [ ] `jit claim release <lease-id>`
- [ ] `jit claim status [--json]`
- [ ] `jit worktree info` (show current worktree context)

### Phase 5: Recovery & Robustness
- [ ] Crash recovery (stale lease cleanup)
- [ ] Claims index rebuild from JSONL
- [ ] Lock file cleanup (PID-based or TTL)
- [ ] Consistency validators

### Phase 6: Documentation
- [ ] Parallel work tutorial
- [ ] Worktree setup guide
- [ ] Claim coordination reference
- [ ] Troubleshooting guide

## Schema Definitions

See attached design document for:
- Claims JSONL schema
- Claims index JSON schema
- Worktree identity file schema
- Heartbeat file schema
- Pre-commit hook template

## Security Considerations
- Use 0700 permissions for `.git/jit/` directories
- Single-user isolation (multi-user requires group permissions)
- Audit trail in append-only log

## Testing Strategy
- Property-based tests for claim coordination
- Concurrent claim acquisition tests
- Lease expiration and eviction tests
- Recovery from crash scenarios
- Hook enforcement validation
title: Enable parallel multi-agent work with git worktrees
